cues.zh: 并被法律政策赋予在若干方面作为个体行事的能力，

cues.en: enjoying privileges and immunities in common and of exercising a variety of political rights more or less extensive according to the design of its institution
cues.zh: 享有共同的豁免权和特权，并根据其制度设计行使程度不一的各种政治权利

cues.en: or the powers conferred upon it, either at the time of its creation or at any subsequent period of of its existence.
cues.zh: 或者赋予它的权力，无论是在其创立之时，还是在其存在的任何后续时期。

cues.en: This was a late eighteenth century definition.
cues.zh: 这是18世纪末的一个定义。

cues.en: Sound like a piece of software to you?
cues.zh: 听起来像是一款软件吗？

cues.en: the British government passed the Joint Stock Companies Act, which created a register of companies and allowed any legal person for a fee to register a company, which in turn existed as a separate legal person.
cues.zh: 英国政府通过了《合股公司法》，设立了公司登记制度，允许任何法人在缴纳费用后注册公司，而公司本身则作为独立法人存在。

cues.en: Prior to that point, it required a royal charter or an act of parliament to create a company.
cues.zh: 在此之前，创建公司需要获得皇家特许状或议会法案的批准。

cues.en: Subsequently, the law was extended to limit the liability of individual shareholders in event of business failure.
cues.zh: 随后，法律扩展到在企业倒闭时限制个人股东的责任。

cues.en: And then both Germany and The United States added their own unique twists to what today we see as the doctrine of corporate personhood.
cues.zh: 然后，德国和美国各自添加了独特的元素，形成了我们今天所看到的公司人格理论。

cues.en: Now there are plenty of other things that happened between the sixteenth and twenty first centuries that changed the shape of the world we live in. I've skipped the changes in agricultural productivity
cues.zh: 从十六世纪到二十一世纪之间，还发生了许多其他改变世界面貌的事情。我跳过了农业生产力方面的变化，

cues.en: that happened due to energy economics,
cues.zh: 这些变化是由能源经济学引起的，

cues.en: which finally broke the Malthusian trap our predecessors lived in.
cues.zh: 最终打破了我们先辈生活的马尔萨斯陷阱。

cues.en: This in turn broke the long term cap on economic growth of about o point 1% per year in the absence of famines, plagues, and wars, and so on.
cues.zh: 这反过来又打破了在没有饥荒、瘟疫和战争等情况下经济年增长约0.1%的长期上限。

cues.en: I've skipped the germ theory of diseases and the development of trade empires in the age of sale and gunpowder
cues.zh: 我跳过了病菌学说以及在航海和火药时代贸易帝国的崛起，

cues.en: that were made possible by advances in accurate time measurement.
cues.zh: 这些帝国的形成得益于精确时间测量的进步。

cues.en: I've skipped the rise and, hopefully, decline
cues.zh: 我跳过了科学种族主义这一有害理论的兴起以及（希望如此）衰落，

cues.en: of the pernicious theory of scientific racism that underpinned Western colonialism and the slave trade.
cues.zh: 这一理论支撑了西方殖民主义和奴隶贸易。

cues.en: I've skipped the rise of feminism, the ideological position that women are human beings rather than property, and the decline of patriarchy.
cues.zh: 我跳过了女权主义的兴起，即女性是人而非财产的意识形态立场，以及父权制的衰落。

cues.en: I've skipped the whole of the enlightenment and the age of revolutions.
cues.zh: 我跳过了整个启蒙运动和革命时代。

cues.en: But this is a technocratic... Technocentric congress. So I wanna frame this talk in terms of AI, which we all like to think we understand.
cues.zh: 但这是一个技术官僚……以技术为中心的会议。所以我想用人工智能的角度来组织这次演讲，我们大家都自以为很懂人工智能。

cues.en: Here's the thing about these artificial persons we call corporations.
cues.zh: 我们称之为公司的这些“人造人”就是这么回事。

cues.en: Legally, they're people.
cues.zh: 从法律上讲，它们就是人。

cues.en: They have goals. They operate in pursuit of these goals.
cues.zh: 它们有目标，它们的运作都是为了追求这些目标。

cues.en: They have a natural life cycle.
cues.zh: 它们有自然的生命周期。

cues.en: In the nineteen fifties, a typical US corporation on the S and P 500 index had a lifespan of sixty years.
cues.zh: 在二十世纪五十年代，标普500指数中的典型美国公司寿命为六十年。

cues.en: Today, it's down to less than twenty years.
cues.zh: 而今天，这一数字已经降到了不到二十年。

cues.en: This is largely due to predation.
cues.zh: 这主要归咎于弱肉强食的掠夺。

cues.en: Corporations are cannibals. They eat one another.
cues.zh: 公司都是食人者，它们互相吞噬。

cues.en: They're also hive superorganisms
cues.zh: 它们也是蜂群一样的超级有机体，

cues.en: like bees or ants.
cues.zh: 就像蜜蜂或蚂蚁一样。

cues.en: For the first century and a half, they relied entirely on human employees for their internal operation,
cues.zh: 在最初的一个半世纪里，它们的内部运作完全依赖人类员工，

cues.en: but today, they're automating their business processes very rapidly.
cues.zh: 但今天，它们正以极快的速度将业务流程自动化。

cues.en: Each human is only retained so long as they can perform their assigned tasks more efficiently than a piece of software,
cues.zh: 每一个人类员工只有在能比软件更高效地完成指派任务时才会留用，

cues.en: and they can all be replaced by another human much as the cells in our own bodies are functionally interchangeable,
cues.zh: 而且每个人都可以被其他人取代，就像我们体内的细胞在功能上是可以互换的一样，

cues.en: and a group of cells can, in extremis, often be replaced by a prosthetic device.
cues.zh: 而且在极端情况下，一组细胞通常可以被假体装置所替代。

cues.en: To some extent, corporations can be trained to serve of the personal desires of their chief executives, but even CEOs can be dispensed with if their activities damage the corporation as Harvey Weinstein found out a couple of months ago.
cues.zh: 在某种程度上，公司可以被调教得去迎合其首席执行官的个人愿望，但正如 Harvey Weinstein 几个月前所发现的那样，如果CEO的行为损害了公司的利益，就连他们也是可以被撤换的。

cues.en: Finally,
cues.zh: 最后，

cues.en: our legal environment today has been tailored for the convenience of corporate persons rather than human persons to the point where our governments now mimic corporations in many of their internal structures.
cues.zh: 如今我们的法律环境是为了公司法人而非自然人的便利而量身定制的，以至于我们的政府在许多内部结构上现在都在模仿公司。

cues.en: So to understand where we're going, we need to start by asking, what do our current actually existing AI overlords want?
cues.zh: 所以要理解我们将走向何方，我们需要先问：我们当前实际存在的AI霸主想要什么？

cues.en: Now, Elon Musk, who I believe you've all heard of, has an obsessive fear of one particular hazard of artificial intelligence,
cues.zh: 埃隆·马斯克，我相信你们都听说过他，他对人工智能的一种特定危险有着执着的恐惧，

cues.en: which he conceives of as being a piece of software that functions like a brain in a box, namely the paper clip optimizer
cues.zh: 他将其设想为一种像盒中大脑一样运作的软件，即回形针优化器

cues.en: or maximizer.
cues.zh: 或最大化器。

cues.en: A paper clip maximizer is a term of art for a goal seeking AI that has a single priority.
cues.zh: 回形针最大化器是一个专业术语，指只有一个优先目标的目标导向型AI。

cues.en: For example, maximizing the number of paper clips in the universe.
cues.zh: 例如，最大化宇宙中回形针的数量。

cues.en: The paper clip maximizer is able to improve itself in pursuit of its goal but has no ability to vary its goal. So it will ultimately attempt to convert all the metallic elements in the solar system into paper clips
cues.zh: 回形针最大化器能够在追求目标的过程中自我改进，但无法改变其目标。所以它最终会试图把太阳系中所有金属元素都转化成回形针

cues.en: even if this is obviously detrimental to the well-being of the humans who set at this goal.
cues.zh: 即使这显然有害于设定这一目标的人类的福祉。

cues.en: Unfortunately,
cues.zh: 不幸的是，

cues.en: I don't think Musk is paying enough attention.
cues.zh: 我认为马斯克没有给予足够的关注。

cues.en: Consider his own companies.
cues.zh: 看看他自己的公司。

cues.en: Tesla isn't a paper clip maximizer. It's a battery maximizer.
cues.zh: 特斯拉不是回形针最大化器。它是电池最大化器。

cues.en: After all, a battery... An electric car is a battery with wheels and seats.
cues.zh: 毕竟，电池……电动汽车就是带轮子和座椅的电池。

cues.en: SpaceX is an orbital payload maximizer,
cues.zh: SpaceX是轨道载荷最大化器，

cues.en: driving down the cost of space launches in order to encourage more sales for the service it provides.
cues.zh: 压低太空发射成本，以促进其提供服务的更多销售。

cues.en: SolarCity is a photovoltaic panel maximizer, and so on. All three of the... Musk's very own slow AIs are based on an architecture designed to maximize return on shareholder investment,
cues.zh: SolarCity是一家光伏面板最大化公司，诸如此类。这三者……马斯克自家的那些慢速AI，都基于一种旨在最大化股东投资回报的架构，

cues.en: even if by doing so, they cook the planet the shareholders have to live on or turn the entire thing into solar panels.
cues.zh: 哪怕这样做会毁掉股东们赖以生存的星球，或者把整个地球都变成太阳能面板。

cues.en: But, hey, if you're Elon Musk, that's okay. You're gonna retire on Mars anyway.
cues.zh: 不过，嘿，如果你是埃隆·马斯克，那也没关系。反正你退休后要去火星。

cues.en: By the way,
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，

cues.en: I'm ragging on Musk in this talk simply because he's the current opinionated tech billionaire who thinks that disrupting a couple of industries entitles him to make headlines.
cues.zh: 我在这次演讲里吐槽马斯克，只是因为他正是当下那位固执己见的科技亿万富翁，自认为颠覆了几个行业就有资格上头条。

cues.en: If this was 2007
cues.zh: 如果现在是2007年，

cues.en: and my focus slightly difference... Different, I'd be ragging on Steve Jobs.
cues.zh: 而我的关注点略有不同……不同的话，我吐槽的就是史蒂夫·乔布斯了。

cues.en: And if we were in 1997,
cues.zh: 如果我们身处1997年，

cues.en: my target would be Bill Gates. Don't take it personally, Elon.
cues.zh: 我的目标就会是比尔·盖茨。别往心里去，埃隆。

cues.en: Back to topic.
cues.zh: 回到正题。

cues.en: The problem with corporations
cues.zh: 企业的问题在于，

cues.en: is that despite their overt goals,
cues.zh: 尽管它们有公开的目标，

cues.en: whether they make electric vehicles or beer or sell life insurance policies, they all have a common implicit paper clip maximizer goal to generate revenue.
cues.zh: 无论是造电动汽车、酿啤酒，还是卖人寿保险，它们都有一个共同的隐性回形针最大化目标：创造收入。

cues.en: If they don't make money, they're eaten by a bigger predator or they go bust.
cues.zh: 如果赚不到钱，它们就会被更大的掠食者吃掉，或者破产。

cues.en: It's as vital to them as breathing is to us mammals.
cues.zh: 这对它们来说，就像呼吸对我们哺乳动物一样至关重要。

cues.en: They generally pursue their implicit goal, maximizing revenue,
cues.zh: 它们通常通过追求公开目标，

cues.en: by pursuing their overt goal.
cues.zh: 来实现其隐性目标——收入最大化。

cues.en: But sometimes they try instead to manipulate their environment
cues.zh: 但有时它们会转而试图操纵环境，

cues.en: to ensure that money flows to them regardless.
cues.zh: 以确保钱无论如何都流向它们。

cues.en: Human tool making culture has become very complicated over time. New technologies always come with an attached implicit political agenda that seeks to extend the use of the technology.
cues.zh: 人类制造工具的文化随着时间推移变得非常复杂。新技术总是附带一种隐含的政治议程，试图扩大该技术的使用范围。

cues.en: Governments react to this by legislating to control new technologies,
cues.zh: 政府对此的反应是通过立法来控制新技术，

cues.en: and sometimes we end up with industries
cues.zh: 有时我们最终会看到一些行业

cues.en: actually indulging in legal duels
cues.zh: 实际上沉迷于法律对决

cues.en: through the regulatory mechanism of law to determine
cues.zh: 通过法律的监管机制来决定

cues.en: who prevails.
cues.zh: 谁占上风。

cues.en: For example, consider the automobile.
cues.zh: 例如，想想汽车。

cues.en: You can't have mass automobile transport without gas stations and fuel distribution pipelines.
cues.zh: 没有加油站和燃料配送管道，就不可能有大规模的汽车运输。

cues.en: These in turn require access to whoever owns the land the oil is extracted from under. And before you know it, you end up with a permanent army in Iraq and a clamned dictatorship in Saudi Arabia.
cues.zh: 这些反过来又需要接触到石油开采所在地的土地所有者。不知不觉中，你就会在伊拉克留下一支永久驻军，在沙特阿拉伯看到一个部族独裁政权。

cues.en: Closer to home,
cues.zh: 更贴近生活的是，

cues.en: automobiles
cues.zh: 汽车

cues.en: imply jaywalking laws and drink driving laws.
cues.zh: 意味着乱穿马路法和酒驾法。

cues.en: They affect town planning regulations and encourage suburban sprawl,
cues.zh: 它们影响城镇规划法规，鼓励郊区蔓延，

cues.en: the construction of human infrastructure on a scale required by automobiles,
cues.zh: 按照汽车所需规模建设人类基础设施，

cues.en: not pedestrians.
cues.zh: 而不是为行人。

cues.en: This in turn is bad for competing transport technologies like buses or trams,
cues.zh: 这反过来又不利于公交车或有轨电车等竞争性交通技术，

cues.en: which work best in cities with a high population density.
cues.zh: 这些技术在高人口密度的城市中效果最好。

cues.en: So to get laws that favor the automobile in place, providing an environment conducive to doing business,
cues.zh: 因此，为了制定有利于汽车的法律，营造有利于经商的环境，

cues.en: automobile companies spent money on political lobbyists,
cues.zh: 汽车公司花钱聘请政治说客，

cues.en: and when they can get away with it, on bribes.
cues.zh: 在能逃脱惩罚时，还会行贿。

cues.en: Bribery needn't be blatant, of course.
cues.zh: 当然，行贿不必明目张胆。

cues.en: For example, the reforms of the British railway network in the 1960s dismembered many branch lines and coincided with a surge in road building and automobile sales.
cues.zh: 例如，20世纪60年代英国铁路网的改革拆除了许多支线铁路，同时公路建设和汽车销量激增。

cues.en: These reforms were orchestrated by transport minister Ernest Marples,
cues.zh: 这些改革由交通部长 Ernest Marples 策划，

cues.en: who was purely a politician.
cues.zh: 他纯粹是个政客。

cues.en: The fact that he accumulated a considerable personal fortune during this period by buying shares in motorway construction corporations
cues.zh: 在此期间，他通过购买高速公路建设公司的股票积累了相当可观的个人财富，

cues.en: has nothing to do with it.
cues.zh: 这和改革毫无关系。

cues.en: So no conflict of interest there.
cues.zh: 所以不存在利益冲突。

cues.en: Now, the automobile industry can't be considered a pure paper clip maximizer.
cues.zh: 现在，汽车产业不能被视为一个纯粹的回形针最大化器。

cues.en: Sorry. The automobile industry in isolation can't be considered a pure paper clip maximizer.
cues.zh: 抱歉。单看汽车产业，不能把它视为一个纯粹的回形针最大化器。

cues.en: You have to look at it in conjunction with the fossil fuel industries,
cues.zh: 你得把它和化石燃料产业放在一起看，

cues.en: the road construction business,
cues.zh: 还有道路建设行业，

cues.en: the accident insurance sector, and so on.
cues.zh: 事故保险行业等等。

cues.en: When you do this, you begin to see the outline of a paper clip maximizing ecosystem
cues.zh: 这样一来，你就开始看出一个回形针最大化生态系统的轮廓，

cues.en: that invades far flung lands and grinds up and kills around one and a quarter million people per year.
cues.zh: 它侵入遥远的土地，每年碾压并导致约125万人死亡。

cues.en: That's the global death toll from automobile accidents currently according to the World Health Organization.
cues.zh: 根据世界卫生组织的数据，这是目前全球汽车事故的死亡人数。

cues.en: It rivals the first world war on an ongoing permanent basis, and these are all side effects of its drive to sell you a new car.
cues.zh: 它持续造成的死亡人数堪比第一次世界大战，而这些全都是它促使你买新车所带来的副作用。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: automobiles aren't, of course, a total liability.
cues.zh: 当然，汽车也并非一无是处。

cues.en: Today's cars are regulated stringently for safety and in theory to reduce toxic emissions.
cues.zh: 如今的汽车受到严格的安全监管，理论上也受到严格监管以减少有毒排放。

cues.en: They're fast, efficient, and comfortable.
cues.zh: 它们又快、又高效，还很舒适。

cues.en: We can thank
cues.zh: 这一切当然要归功于

cues.en: legal mandated regulations
cues.zh: 法律强制执行的法规，

cues.en: imposed by governments for this, of course.
cues.zh: 也就是政府推行的监管政策。

cues.en: Go back to the nineteen seventies and cars didn't have crumple zones.
cues.zh: 回到 20 世纪 70 年代，汽车连溃缩吸能区都没有。

cues.en: Go back to the fifties, and they didn't come with seat belts as standard.
cues.zh: 回到 50 年代，安全带甚至还不是标配。

cues.en: In the nineteen thirties, indicators, turn signals, and brakes on all four wheels were optional.
cues.zh: 在 20 世纪 30 年代，转向指示器、转向灯以及四轮刹车都还是选配件。

cues.en: And your best hope of surviving a 50 kilometer per hour crash was to be thrown out of a car and land somewhere without breaking your neck.
cues.zh: 要想在时速 50 公里的车祸中活下来，你最大的希望是被甩出车外，落地时没摔断脖子。

cues.en: Regulatory agencies are our current political system's tool of choice for preventing paperclip maximizers from running amok.
cues.zh: 监管机构是当前政治体系的首选工具，用来防止“回形针最大化者”肆意妄为。

cues.en: Unfortunately,
cues.zh: 不幸的是，

cues.en: regulators don't always work.
cues.zh: 监管并不总是管用。

cues.en: The first failure mode of regulators that you need to be aware of is regulatory capture,
cues.zh: 你需要注意的监管机构的第一种失效模式，就是“监管俘获”，

cues.en: where regulatory bodies are captured by the industries they control.
cues.zh: 即监管机构反过来被其所监管的行业所掌控。

cues.en: Ajit Pai, head of the American Federal Communications Commission,
cues.zh: 美国 Federal Communications Commission 的主席 Ajit Pai，

cues.en: which just voted to eliminate net neutrality rules in The United States,
cues.zh: 该机构刚刚投票废除了美国的网络中立性规则，

cues.en: has worked as associate general counsel for Verizon Communications
cues.zh: 他曾担任过 Verizon Communications 的副总法律顾问，

cues.en: Inc, the largest current descendant of the Bell Telephone Systems monopoly.
cues.zh: 而该公司正是 Bell Telephone Systems 垄断帝国如今最大的延续者。

cues.en: After the AT and T antitrust lawsuit,
cues.zh: 在 AT&T 反垄断诉讼之后，

cues.en: the Bell Network was broken up into the seven baby bells. They've now pretty much reformed and re aggregated, and Verizon is the largest current one.
cues.zh: Bell 网络被拆分成了七家“Baby Bells”。如今它们基本重新抱团整合，而 Verizon 是目前最大的一家。

cues.en: Why should someone with a transparent
cues.zh: 为什么一个对某家科技巨头有着显而易见

cues.en: interest in a technology corporation end up running a regulator that tries to control the industry in question? Well, if you're going to regulate a complex technology, you need to recruit regulators from people who understand it.
cues.zh: 利益关联的人，最终会去掌管试图监管该行业的机构？因为要监管一项复杂技术，你就必须从懂它的人当中招募监管者。

cues.en: Unfortunately, most of those people are industry insiders.
cues.zh: 遗憾的是，这些人大多是业内人士。

cues.en: Ajit Pai is clearly very much aware of how Verizon is regulated,
cues.zh: Ajit Pai显然非常清楚Verizon是如何被监管的，

cues.en: very insightful into its operations, and wants to do something about it, just not necessarily in the public interest.
cues.zh: 对其运营有着深刻的洞察，并且想要对此采取行动，只是未必符合公众利益。

cues.en: When
cues.zh: 当

cues.en: regulators end up staffed by people drawn from the industries they're supposed to control,
cues.zh: 监管机构最终由来自他们本应控制的行业的人填充时，

cues.en: they frequently end up working with their former office mates to make it easier to turn a profit,
cues.zh: 他们常常与以前的同事合作，让盈利变得更容易，

cues.en: either by raising barriers to keep new insurgent companies out or by dismantling safeguards that protect the public.
cues.zh: 要么通过提高门槛将新兴的公司挡在外面，要么通过拆除保护公众的保障措施。

cues.en: Now
cues.zh: 现在

cues.en: a second problem is regulatory lag,
cues.zh: 第二个问题是监管滞后，

cues.en: where a technology advances so rapidly that regulations are laughably obsolete by the time they're issued.
cues.zh: 即技术发展如此迅速，以至于法规在发布时已经过时得可笑。

cues.en: Consider the EU directive requiring cookie notices on websites caution users that their activities are tracked and their privacy may be violated.
cues.zh: 想想欧盟的指令，要求网站在网站上放置cookie通知，提醒用户他们的活动被跟踪，隐私可能被侵犯。

cues.en: This would have been a good idea in 1993 or 1996,
cues.zh: 这在1993年或1996年是个好主意，

cues.en: but unfortunately, it didn't show up until 2011.
cues.zh: 但不幸的是，直到2011年才出现。

cues.en: Fingerprinting and tracking mechanisms had nothing to do with cookies and were already widespread by then.
cues.zh: 指纹识别和跟踪机制与cookie无关，那时已经广泛存在。

cues.en: Tim Berners Lee observed in 1995
cues.zh: Tim Berners Lee在1995年观察到

cues.en: that five years' worth of change was happening on the web for every twelve months of real world time. By that yardstick, the cookie law came out nearly a century too late to do any good.
cues.zh: 网络上每十二个月现实世界时间就发生五年的变化。按照这个标准，cookie法律出台晚了近一个世纪，无法发挥任何作用。

cues.en: Again, look at Uber.
cues.zh: 再次，看看Uber。

cues.en: This month, the European Court of Justice ruled that Uber is a taxi service, not a web app. This is arguably correct. The problem is Uber has spread globally since it was founded eight years ago, subsidizing its drivers to put competing private hire firms out of business.
cues.zh: 本月，欧洲法院裁定Uber是出租车服务，而不是网络应用。这可以说正确。问题是Uber自八年前成立以来已在全球蔓延，补贴司机让竞争的私人租车公司倒闭。

cues.en: Whether this is a net good for society is arg... Is debatable. The problem is a taxi driver can get awfully hungry if she has to wait eight years for court ruling against a predator intent on disrupting her business.
cues.zh: 这是否对社会有净好处……还有待商榷。问题是，如果出租车司机要等上八年才能等到法院对那个一心扰乱她生意的掠夺者作出裁决，她会饿得不行。

cues.en: So to recap,
cues.zh: 那么总结一下，

cues.en: firstly, we already have paper clip maximizers,
cues.zh: 首先，我们已经有回形针最大化器了，

cues.en: and Musk's AI alarmism is curiously mirror blind.
cues.zh: 而马斯克对AI的危言耸听，奇怪地对此视而不见。

cues.en: Secondly,
cues.zh: 其次，

cues.en: we have mechanisms for keeping paper clip maximizers in check, but they don't work very well against AIs that deploy the dark arts, especially corruption and bribery,
cues.zh: 我们有制约回形针最大化器的机制，但这些机制对那些施展暗黑手段的AI——尤其是腐败和贿赂——效果不佳，

cues.en: and they're even worse against true AIs that evolve too fast for human mediated mechanisms like the law to keep up with.
cues.zh: 面对真正的AI更是如此，它们进化得太快，像法律这样的人类介导机制根本跟不上。

cues.en: Finally,
cues.zh: 最后，

cues.en: unlike the naive vision of a paper clip maximizer that maximizes only paper clips,
cues.zh: 不同于回形针最大化器只最大化回形针的朴素设想，

cues.en: existing AIs have multiple agendas.
cues.zh: 现有的AI有多重议程。

cues.en: Their overt goal, but also profit seeking,
cues.zh: 它们有公开的目标，同时也在逐利、

cues.en: expansion into new markets,
cues.zh: 扩张新市场、

cues.en: and to accommodate the desire of whoever is currently in the driving seat.
cues.zh: 并迎合当前掌舵者的意愿。

cues.en: Now, this brings me to the next major heading in this
cues.zh: 现在，这让我想到这份

cues.en: dismaying laundry list, how it all went wrong.
cues.zh: 令人沮丧的清单上的下一个主要标题：一切是如何出错的。

cues.en: It seems to me that our current political upheavals are best understood as arriving... As arising
cues.zh: 在我看来，我们当前的政治动荡最好理解为源于……

cues.en: from the capture of post 1917 democratic institutions by large scale AI.
cues.zh: 源于1917年后的民主制度被大规模AI所俘获。

cues.en: Everywhere you look, you see voters protesting angrily against an entrenched establishment
cues.zh: 放眼望去，到处都是选民愤怒地抗议一个根深蒂固的建制派，

cues.en: that seems determined to ignore the wants and needs of their human constituents in favor of those of the machines.
cues.zh: 这个建制派似乎决心无视人类选民的诉求和需要，转而迎合机器的诉求。

cues.en: The Brexit upset was largely the result of a protest vote against the British political establishment.
cues.zh: 英国脱欧的震荡，很大程度上是对英国政治体制的抗议投票的结果。

cues.en: The election of Donald Trump, likewise, with a side order of racism on top.
cues.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普的当选同样如此，还外加一层种族主义色彩。

cues.en: Our major political parties are led by people who are compatible with the system as it exists today,
cues.zh: 我们的主要政党由那些与当今现有体制相容的人领导，

cues.en: a system that has been shaped over decades
cues.zh: 这个体制历经数十年塑造，

cues.en: by corporations distorting our government and regulatory environments.
cues.zh: 由企业扭曲我们的政府和监管环境而成。

cues.en: We humans live in a world shaped by the desires and needs of AI, forced to live on their terms. And we're taught that we're valuable only to the extent we contribute to the rule of the machines.
cues.zh: 我们人类生活在一个由AI的欲望和需求所塑造的世界里，被迫按照它们的条件生活。我们被教导说，只有在对机器的统治做出贡献的程度上，我们才有价值。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: this is three c, and we're all more interested in computers and communications technology than this historical crap.
cues.zh: 这是三个C，我们都对计算机和通信技术更感兴趣，而不是这些历史废话。

cues.en: But as I said earlier, history is a secret weapon if you know how to use it.
cues.zh: 但正如我之前所说，历史是一件秘密武器，如果你知道如何使用它的话。

cues.en: What history is good for is enabling us to spot recurring patterns that repeat across time scales outside our personal experience.
cues.zh: 历史的好处在于，它能让我们发现那些在我们个人经验之外的时间尺度上反复出现的模式。

cues.en: And if we look at our historical very slow AIs, what do we learn from them about modern AI and how it's going to behave?
cues.zh: 如果我们审视历史上那些非常缓慢的AI，我们能从它们身上学到什么关于现代AI及其行为方式的东西？

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: to start with, our AIs have been warped. The new AIs, the electronic ones instantiated in our machines, have been warped by a terrible fundamentally flawed design decision back in 1995
cues.zh: 首先，我们的AI已经被扭曲了。新的AI，那些在我们的机器中实例化的电子AI，已经被1995年一个可怕的、根本上有缺陷的设计决策所扭曲，

cues.en: that has damaged democratic political processes,
cues.zh: 这个决策损害了民主政治进程，

cues.en: crippled our ability to truly understand the world around us, and led to the angry upheavals and upsets of the present decade.
cues.zh: 削弱了我们真正理解周围世界的能力，并导致了当前这十年愤怒的动荡和混乱。

cues.en: That mistake
cues.zh: 那个错误

cues.en: was the decision to fund the build out of a public worldwide web as opposed to the earlier government funded corporate and academic Internet
cues.zh: 就是决定出资建设一个面向公众的万维网，而不是早先由政府资助的企业和学术互联网

cues.en: by monetizing eyeballs through advertising revenue.
cues.zh: 通过广告收入将眼球流量变现。

cues.en: The ad supported web we're used to today wasn't inevitable.
cues.zh: 我们今天习以为常的广告支持型网络并非必然。

cues.en: If you recall the web as it was in 1994,
cues.zh: 如果你还记得1994年的网络是什么样子，

cues.en: there were very few ads at all and not much in the way of commerce.
cues.zh: 那时几乎没有广告，商业活动也不多。

cues.en: was the year the World Wide Web really came to public attention in the Anglophone world, and consumer facing websites began to appear.
cues.zh: 是万维网在英语世界真正引起公众关注的一年，面向消费者的网站开始出现。

cues.en: Nobody really knew how this thing was going to be paid for. The original .com bubble was all about working out how to monetize the web for the first time, and a lot of people lost their shirts in the process.
cues.zh: 当时没人真正知道这东西该怎么盈利。最初的.com泡沫就是围绕如何第一次把网络变现展开的，很多人在这个过程中赔得精光。

cues.en: Our naive initial assumption
cues.zh: 我们最初天真的假设

cues.en: was that the transaction cost of setting up a TCP IP connection over modem was too high to support... To be supported by per use micro billing for web pages.
cues.zh: 是：通过调制解调器建立TCP/IP连接的事务成本太高，无法支撑……无法支撑按每次使用对网页进行微额计费。

cues.en: So instead of charging people a fraction of a euro cent for every page view, we'd bill customers indirectly
cues.zh: 所以，与其对每次页面浏览向用户收取几分之一欧分，我们选择间接向客户收费

cues.en: by shoving advert... Advertising banners in front of their eyes and hoping they'd click through and buy something.
cues.zh: 方式是硬塞广告……把广告横幅推到他们眼前，希望他们点击并购买东西。

cues.en: Unfortunately,
cues.zh: 不幸的是，

cues.en: advertising is in an industry,
cues.zh: 广告是一个行业，

cues.en: one of those preexisting very slow AI ecosystems I already alluded to.
cues.zh: 是我已经提到过的那些早已存在、非常缓慢的AI生态系统之一。

cues.en: Advertising tries to maximize its hold on the attention of the minds behind each human eyeball.
cues.zh: 广告试图最大化对每个人类眼球背后心智的注意力掌控。

cues.en: The coupling of advertising with web search was an inevitable outgrowth. I mean, how better to attract the attention of reluctant subjects than to find out what they're really interested in seeing and selling ads that relate to those interests?
cues.zh: 广告与网络搜索的结合是必然的产物。我的意思是，还有什么比了解那些不情愿的对象真正想看什么，并投放与他们兴趣相关的广告，更能吸引他们的注意力呢？

cues.en: The problem of applying the paper clip maximizer approach to monopolizing eyeballs, however, is that eyeballs are a limited scarce resource.
cues.zh: 然而，将回形针最大化器的方法应用于垄断眼球的问题在于，眼球是一种有限的稀缺资源。

cues.en: There are only a hundred and sixty eight hours in every week in which I can gaze at banner ads.
cues.zh: 每周只有一百六十八个小时，我可以盯着横幅广告。

cues.en: Moreover, most ads are irrelevant to my interests. And it doesn't matter how often you flash an ad for dog biscuits at me, I'm never going to buy any. I have a cat.
cues.zh: 此外，大多数广告与我的兴趣无关。而且，无论你向我闪现多少次狗饼干广告，我都不会买。我有一只猫。

cues.en: To make best revenue generating use of our eyeballs,
cues.zh: 为了最大化利用我们的眼球来创造收入，

cues.en: it's necessary for the ad industry to learn who we are and what interests us and to target us increasingly minutely in hope of hooking us with stuff we're attracted to.
cues.zh: 广告行业必须了解我们是谁、我们的兴趣是什么，并越来越精细地定位我们，希望用我们感兴趣的东西吸引我们。

cues.en: In other words, the ad industry is a paper clip maximizer that for its success relies on developing a theory of mind that applies to human beings.
cues.zh: 换句话说，广告行业是一个回形针最大化器，其成功依赖于发展出一种适用于人类的心理理论。

cues.en: Do I need to divert onto the impassion rant about the hideous corruption and evil that is Facebook?
cues.zh: 我需要转到关于Facebook的丑陋腐败和邪恶的激情 rant 吗？

cues.en: Okay. Somebody said yes. I'm guessing you've heard it all before, but the too long don't read summary is Facebook is as much a search engine as Google or Amazon.
cues.zh: 好的。有人说需要。我猜你们以前都听过，但长话短说的总结是，Facebook和Google或Amazon一样，都是一个搜索引擎。

cues.en: Facebook searches are optimized for faces,
cues.zh: Facebook的搜索是针对面孔优化的，

cues.en: that is for human beings.
cues.zh: 也就是针对人类。

cues.en: If you want to find someone you fell out of touch with thirty years ago, Facebook probably knows where they live, what their favorite color is, what size shoes they wear, and what they said about you to your friends behind your back all those years ago that made you cut them off.
cues.zh: 如果你想找到三十年前失去联系的人，Facebook 大概知道他们住哪儿、喜欢什么颜色、穿多大鞋，还知道当年他们背着你跟你朋友说了什么，让你和他们断了交。

cues.en: Even if you don't have a Facebook account, Facebook has a You account,
cues.zh: 就算你没有 Facebook 账号，Facebook 也有一个“你”的账号，

cues.en: a hole in their social graph with a bunch of connections pointing into it and your name tagged in your friends' photographs.
cues.zh: 在他们的社交图谱里，有一个空洞，一堆连接指向它，你朋友的照片里还标记着你的名字。

cues.en: They know a lot about you, and they sell access to their social graph to advertisers who then target you even if you don't think you use Facebook.
cues.zh: 他们对你了解很多，还把社交图谱的访问权卖给广告商，广告商就能精准投放，哪怕你以为自己不用 Facebook。

cues.en: Indeed, there's barely any point in not using Facebook these days. They're the social media borg. Resistance is futile.
cues.zh: 说实话，如今不用 Facebook 几乎没什么意义。他们是社交媒体博格。抵抗是徒劳的。

cues.en: So,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: however, Facebook is trying to get eyeballs on ads, so is Twitter, and so are Google. To do this, they fine tune the content they show you to make it more attractive to your eyes. And by attractive, I do not mean pleasant.
cues.zh: 不过，Facebook 想让眼球盯住广告，Twitter 也是，Google 也是。为此，他们微调展示给你的内容，让它更吸引你的眼球。而所谓吸引，我指的不是令人愉悦。

cues.en: We humans have an evolved automatic reflex to pay attention to threats and horrors as well as pleasurable stimuli.
cues.zh: 我们人类进化出了一种自动反射，会关注威胁和恐怖的东西，也会关注愉悦的刺激。

cues.en: And the algorithms determine what they show us when we look at Facebook or Twitter take this bias into account.
cues.zh: 而算法在决定我们刷 Facebook 或 Twitter 时展示什么内容时，会把这个偏好考虑进去。

cues.en: You may act... Might react more strongly to a public hanging in Iran or an outrageous statement by Donald Trump than to a couple kissing. The algorithm knows and will show you whatever makes you pay attention,
cues.zh: 你可能……可能对伊朗的公开绞刑或 Donald Trump 的离谱言论反应更强烈，而不是一对接吻的情侣。算法知道这一点，会给你看任何能让你停下眼球的内容，

cues.en: not necessarily what you need or want to see.
cues.zh: 未必是你需要或想看到的东西。

cues.en: So this brings me to another point about computerized AI as opposed to corporate AI.
cues.zh: 所以这引出了我关于计算机化AI与企业化AI的另一个观点。

cues.en: AI algorithms tend to embody the prejudices and beliefs of either the programmers
cues.zh: AI算法往往体现了程序员的偏见和信念

cues.en: or the dataset the AI was trained on.
cues.zh: 或者AI训练所用数据集的偏见和信念。

cues.en: A couple of years ago, I ran across an account of a webcam developed by mostly pale skinned Silicon Valley engineers that had difficulty focusing or achieving correct color balance when pointed at dark skinned faces.
cues.zh: 几年前，我偶然看到一篇报道，说主要由肤色较浅的硅谷工程师开发的网络摄像头，在对着深色皮肤的面孔时，很难对焦或达到正确的色彩平衡。

cues.en: That's an example of human programmer induced bias. They didn't have a wide enough test set and didn't recognize
cues.zh: 这就是人类程序员引入偏见的一个例子。他们没有足够广泛的测试集，也没有意识到

cues.en: that they were inherently biased towards expect... Expecting people to have pale skin.
cues.zh: 自己本身就带有偏见，期望……期望人们拥有浅色皮肤。

cues.en: But with today's deep learning, bias can creep in via the datasets the neural networks are trained on
cues.zh: 但在当今的深度学习中，偏见可以通过神经网络训练所用的数据集悄然渗入

cues.en: even without the programmers intending it.
cues.zh: 即使程序员并无此意。

cues.en: Microsoft's first foray into a conversational chatbot driven by machine learning, Tay, was what we yanked offline within days last year because four channel Reddit based trolls discovered that they could train it towards racism and sexism for shits and giggles.
cues.zh: 微软首次涉足由机器学习驱动的对话式聊天机器人Tay，去年上线没几天就被我们下线了，因为4chan上那些Reddit的喷子发现，他们可以为了好玩把它训练得充满种族主义和性别歧视。

cues.en: Just imagine, you're a poor naive innocent AI
cues.zh: 想象一下，你是一个可怜、天真、无辜的AI

cues.en: who's just been switched on and you're hoping to pass your Turing test and what happens?
cues.zh: 刚刚被开机，你满心希望能通过图灵测试，结果发生了什么？

cues.en: For Chan decide to to play with your head.
cues.zh: 有人决定来玩弄你的大脑。

cues.en: I got to feel sorry for today.
cues.zh: 我都有点同情今天的AI了。

cues.en: Now
cues.zh: 现在

cues.en: humans may be biased, but at least individually we're accountable.
cues.zh: 人类可能有偏见，但至少我们每个人都要负责任。

cues.en: And if somebody gives you racist or sexist abuse to your face, you can complain or maybe punch them.
cues.zh: 如果有人当面用种族主义或性别歧视的话语辱骂你，你可以投诉，或者干脆揍他一顿。

cues.en: It's impossible to punch a corporation,
cues.zh: 你没法揍一家公司，

cues.en: and it may not even be possible to identify the source of unfair bias when you're dealing with a machine learning system.
cues.zh: 而且当你面对一个机器学习系统时，甚至可能无法找出不公平偏见的来源。

cues.en: AI based systems that instantiate existing prejudices
cues.zh: 基于AI的系统会固化已有的偏见，

cues.en: make social change harder.
cues.zh: 让社会变革更加困难。

cues.en: Traditional advertising works by playing on the target customer's insecurity and fear as much as their aspirations,
cues.zh: 传统广告的运作方式，是利用目标客户的不安全感和恐惧，不亚于利用他们的渴望，

cues.en: and fear of loss of social status and privileges are powerful threats.
cues.zh: 而对失去社会地位和特权的恐惧是强有力的威胁。

cues.en: Fear and xenophobia are useful tools for attracting advertising.
cues.zh: 恐惧和排外情绪是吸引广告的有用工具。

cues.en: Eyeballs.
cues.zh: 眼球。

cues.en: What happens when we get pervasive social networks with learned biases against, say, feminism or Islam or melanin
cues.zh: 当我们拥有无处不在的社交网络，带着习得的偏见——比如针对女权主义、伊斯兰教或肤色的偏见——会发生什么？

cues.en: or deep learning systems trained on datasets contaminated by racist dipshits and their propaganda.
cues.zh: 又或者，深度学习系统是在被种族主义蠢货及其宣传污染的数据集上训练出来的。

cues.en: Deep learning systems like the ones inside Facebook that determine which stories to show you to get you to pay as much attention as possible to the adverts.
cues.zh: 像Facebook内部那样的深度学习系统，决定给你展示哪些内容，好让你尽可能多地关注广告。

cues.en: I think you probably have an inkling of how... Where this is now going.
cues.zh: 我想你大概已经隐约感觉到……接下来要往哪儿走了。

cues.en: Now
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: if you think this is sounding a bit bleak and unpleasant, you'd be right.
cues.zh: 如果你觉得这听起来有点悲观和令人不快，你说得对。

cues.en: I write sci fi. You read or watch or play sci fi. We're acculturated to think of science and technology as good things that make life better,
